content.text: The text combines excerpts on English gardening, the Lower Canada rebellions, Maya–Egyptian comparisons, and a moral adventure story. The gardening essays celebrate flowers, orchards, landscape design, horticulturists, and writers including Bacon, Milton, Pope, and Evelyn. The history recounts the 1837–38 Patriote uprisings: battles at St Denis, St Charles, St Eustache, Moore’s Corners, Lacolle, and Odelltown; defeats, executions, burnings, Durham’s amnesty, and his influential report advocating responsible government. The Maya essay argues—speculatively—for ancient connections between Maya, Egyptian, Asian, and African religion, language, astronomy, customs, and monuments. In the fiction, Dan travels to Jersey City and a Cunard steamer, recovers stolen money, exposes a counterfeit passer, and brings Althea home. He moves with his mother and Althea to West Sixteenth Street, becomes a clerk-detective, discovers Talbot’s burglary plot in Houston Street, and alerts Barton and Rogers.
